clue.text: Buyer's recommendation to persuade enrolment in bespoke AA cover

indicators.note: enrolment means being signed up inside something, so one piece is placed within the other
bespoke means made to order, so these letters are made up afresh into a new arrangement

parts.note: to tempt someone is to persuade or entice them

explanation.surface: Advice to a shopper about signing up for a tailored motoring breakdown policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bespoke' rearranges AA COVER into CAVEAOR, and 'enrolment in' puts TEMPT inside it. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown-cover provider.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin maxim means 'let the purchaser beware', a warning given to anyone about to make a purchase.

clue.text: Spell 'amulet'

definitions.meaning: a spell is a magical incantation
an amulet is a lucky trinket worn for protection

explanation.definitionFit: A magic incantation and a protective trinket worn for luck are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Service scooters, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: Vespas are a famous Italian make of motor scooter

explanation.surface: A garage offers a maintenance service for motor scooters.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent VESPAS and the evening church service sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening prayer is a church service held in the late afternoon or evening.

clue.text: It's a river trip for social climber

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall over into a new order

parts.note: taken as the letters of it is, contracted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river cruise is just the thing for someone eager to rise in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey on the river, but it signals that IT'S A RIVER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart who has recently gained wealth or status and is pushing to be accepted by high society.

clue.text: See 1 across
Events providing charcuterie for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the spoken word, so a word of identical sound is wanted

parts.note: charcuterie is cured cold cuts such as ham and salami

explanation.surface: Gatherings at which cold cuts are served to the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting fixtures such as athletics competitions are events.

clue.text: Road not adapted for poor weather

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A road not made ready for bad conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is extreme bad weather.

clue.text: One's pudding follows, say, never over, as a cold dish will be enjoyed

definitions.text: as a cold dish will be enjoyed

indicators.note: follows means the following pieces come after the first part
over means turned back, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
taken as written
one's read as one is, giving the word is
a sweet is a dessert or pudding

explanation.surface: Someone's dessert comes next, a cold dish that will always be relished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EG and NEVER, giving REVEN and GE in answer order. The proverb says revenge is a dish best served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that retribution gives pleasure, like a cold dish that is best savoured.

clue.text: Not easy to accept abbreviated answer in parliamentary report

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: something not easy is hard

indicators.note: abbreviated means shortened, so the word loses its closing letters

parts.note: taken as the whole word before it is shortened

explanation.surface: A tricky short reply recorded in the records of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The official verbatim record of debates in the British Parliament bears this name.

clue.text: Finally in Covid, the leadership party is corrupt

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the following words

parts.note: a rave is a large lively dance party

explanation.surface: A complaint that partying by those in power during the pandemic was corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls UK lockdown parties; the last letters of Covid, the, leadership give DEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is to pervert or debase someone morally.

clue.text: Make sharp political group upset by sexy lure

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen a blade

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the word is read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a party is a political group

explanation.surface: A political faction is thrown into turmoil by a seductive trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme in which a seductive person entices a target into a compromising situation.

clue.text: Teflon-coated Rev out among the godless

indicators.note: among means set within the others, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: impious means lacking reverence for God

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slippery clergyman living with unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the clergyman's title and 'among' sets it inside the word for godless. Teflon is a non-stick coating, so a 'Teflon' politician is one to whom no scandal sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-stick is resistant to anything penetrating or clinging to it.

clue.text: Isn't common parlance used in plain text?

indicators.note: used in means the letters are found within the words given

explanation.surface: A question about whether a colloquialism belongs in plain writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial contraction is the informal, everyday substitute for is not.

clue.text: Haven of love in status quo

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like O
status quo means things as they stand, as is

explanation.surface: A refuge of affection in an unchanging situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, or figuratively any place of calm refuge.

clue.text: Rude attempt to curry favour after 1 Down

definitions.meaning: rude here means insulting or causing offence

definitions.text: attempt to curry favour after 1 Down
definitions.meaning: a word that follows the 1 Down solution in a phrase for a campaign of flattery

explanation.definitionFit: Insulting behaviour is one sense; joined after the spell solution, it completes the phrase for a campaign to win people over.

clue.text: Worker's tactic to steal emcee's heart

indicators.note: to steal here means to take the place of the centre letter

parts.note: an emcee is a master of ceremonies
a ploy is a cunning tactic

explanation.surface: A staff member's scheme to win the presenter's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of EMCEE is C; PLOY replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on a payroll who works for someone else is a worker.

clue.text: Tasteful friend with what she may need to eat

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

parts.words: what she may need to eat
parts.note: a person eating a meal may need a table

explanation.surface: A tactful friend and the thing she may need for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is pleasant to taste is agreeable to the palate.

clue.text: American leader, strong, well-spoken and prosperous

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud and strong
fluent means speaking easily and well

explanation.surface: A powerful, articulate and wealthy US leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and well-off; rich people are prosperous.

clue.text: Continual, not on/off, and mad

indicators.note: off means disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A switch that keeps going on and off, apparently crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' removes ON from CONTINUAL, leaving CTINUAL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An insane person, and by extension anything crazy or mad.

clue.text: See 21 down
Looking safe at last in old capital

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Peking is the former Western name for Beijing, China's capital

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Glancing around to see the strongbox finally in the former Chinese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeping or glancing quickly is a way of looking.

clue.text: Soon to be unidentifiable

definitions.meaning: soon in the archaic sense of shortly or presently
short for anonymous, said of a writer whose name is unknown

explanation.definitionFit: It is an old word for shortly, and also short for anonymous, describing an author left unnamed.

clue.text: Once again, avail yourself of map to find a drink

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially a nautical one
to use something again is to reuse it

explanation.surface: Advice to consult the map again to find somewhere to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the second piece first; the charade runs in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A green or yellow French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Wolf of Canvey Island half seen at the top by you and me

indicators.note: half here takes the first half of each of the two words

parts.note: something at the top is up
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: A wolf from the Essex island, half-spotted on the summit near us.
explanation.walkthrough: The first halves of CANVEY and ISLAND are CAN and ISL. Canvey Island is a town on the Thames estuary in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the scientific Latin name for the grey wolf.

clue.text: See 7
Litter gear sent out

parts.note: kit means equipment or gear

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rubbish and equipment dispatched elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a brood of young animals, such as young cats born together.

clue.text: Forced to be grateful

definitions.meaning: forced means compelled by duty or law
much ... means thankful for a favour

explanation.definitionFit: It means compelled by duty, and also thankful, as in much indebted to someone.

clue.text: Obesity is what NHS patients suffer from, according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: patients of the National Health Service often endure a long delay for treatment

explanation.surface: Being overweight is, it is said, what patients in Britain's health service endure.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, notorious for long waiting lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying too many pounds above a healthy level is the plain description of being heavily overweight.
